The Evidence Packet: the location records relied on above, and how they were compared.

paragraphs.text: I am Maria Delarmo, the defendant in this action. I reside at 2100 WHITE PLAINS ROAD, Bronx, NY 10462. I make this affidavit in support of my application to vacate the default judgment entered against me.

An affidavit of service has been filed in this action. It states that service was made upon me by T. Ockham-Doyle on June 12, 2025 at 7:42 PM, at 2100 WHITE PLAINS ROAD, Bronx, NY 10462, by delivery to a person of suitable age and discretion, and mailing, under CPLR 308(2). A copy is annexed as Exhibit A.
I was not served with the summons and complaint in this action. No papers were delivered to me on June 12, 2025, and I did not learn of this action until long after that date.
2100 WHITE PLAINS ROAD, Bronx, NY 10462, the address at which service is claimed, was not my dwelling place, my usual place of abode or my place of business on that date.
I keep a location history. The records I rely on below are recorded stays in one place. They are annexed as part of Exhibit B, in full for the hours around the time sworn to.

My location history records me in one place from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on June 12, 2025, which includes 7:42 PM, the time of the service sworn to. That place is 10.6 km from 2100 WHITE PLAINS ROAD, Bronx, NY 10462.

The affidavit describes the person who accepted the papers as male, aged 56 to 66 and 5'11" to 6'3". That is not a description of me, and it is not a description of anyone else living at that address.

The comparison of my location records with the affidavit of service, the distances and times relied on above, and the method by which they were calculated, are set out in the Evidence Packet annexed as Exhibit B.
On these facts the court did not acquire personal jurisdiction over me, and the judgment entered against me should be vacated under CPLR 5015(a)(4).

In the alternative, I was served, if at all, by delivery to a person of suitable age and discretion, and mailing, under CPLR 308(2), and not by personal delivery. I did not personally receive notice of this action in time to defend it. I have a meritorious defence to this action: I never opened an account with this company. I therefore ask the court to allow me to defend under CPLR 317.
That application is made within the time allowed, which runs to March 14, 2027.
Because the facts of service are disputed, I respectfully request a traverse hearing at which the process server may be examined.
I respectfully request that enforcement of the judgment, including any restraint on my bank account or wages, be stayed while this application is decided.

A process server licensed in New York City must carry a device that electronically records the location, date and time of every service and every attempt. I respectfully request that the plaintiff be directed to produce that record for the service and attempts described in the affidavit of service.

deadlines.note: If you were served in any way other than in person, and you did not personally get notice in time to defend the case, you may be able to ask the court to reopen it within one year of learning about the judgment, and no more than five years after it was entered. You also have to show you have a defence worth hearing. For you that is one year after you found out, which is March 14, 2027 and five years after the judgment was entered, which is August 1, 2030. The earlier of the two is the one that matters. A judgment can be reopened when the court did not have jurisdiction, which includes service that was not done properly. There is no stated one-year limit for that ground, but act promptly.

findings.detail: Your location history has you in one place from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on June 12, 2025, and that place is 10.6 km from the address on the affidavit. The service claimed at 7:42 PM on June 12, 2025 falls inside that stay.
findings.title: Your phone was somewhere else at that time

findings.detail: The affidavit says the papers were left with someone else at your address, and describes that person as male, aged 56 to 66 and 5'11" to 6'3". That does not match any of the 2 people you listed.
findings.legal_ref: CPLR 308(2) — delivery to a person of suitable age and discretion, and mailing
findings.title: Nobody in your household matches that description

packet.fixes_note: All 19 location records used in this check are listed. They are the records close in time to the sworn moments above; the rest of your location history was never sent off the device it was read on.
packet.intro: This packet compares the affidavit of service filed against Maria Delarmo, index number CV-025236-25/BX, with the location records you supplied. It sets out what the affidavit claims, what your records show, and where the two cannot both be true. It draws no conclusion about what happened, and it is not a finding of fact.

verdict.claimed: The affidavit swears that you were served at 7:42 PM on June 12, 2025 at 2100 WHITE PLAINS ROAD, Bronx, NY 10462, by delivery to a person of suitable age and discretion, and mailing, under CPLR 308(2).
verdict.headline: Your location data conflicts with the affidavit.
verdict.label: Conflicts
verdict.line: Your nearest location record is 10.6 km from that address.
verdict.meaning: Your own records put you away from the address on the affidavit at the time the server swore to, by more than the margins set out under “How this was worked out”.
